findings.description: Phantom Wall illustration is generic and underworked: a flat wall with scattered dots, and a translucent circle overlapping the crenellations that reads as an unintended lens/moon artifact rather than composed art.

The environment is a flat vertical-striped chartreuse gradient — wallpaper, not a tabletop. Cards cast soft shadows onto an abstract plane, undermining the manufactured-object-on-a-surface premise the staging implies.

A dark backing layer protrudes as a visible step above the top edge behind the rail (top-right, repeated on the cast frame). Because it half-emerges only at one corner it reads as a misregistered layer at 2x rather than a deliberate offset-spine motif.

Back composition is sparse: incomplete/asymmetric corner brackets and floating comma-like swashes that are not anchored to the emblem geometry; feels like a wireframe of a back rather than a finished one.

Sunburst ray texture runs directly beneath body text, adding low-level luminance noise behind letterforms; contrast still passes but the panel would be cleaner with the rays masked out of the text measure.
Stat chips are mismatched in visual weight (amber hexagon vs larger maroon circle), and the slashed-zero mono numerals clash with the book-serif voice of the rest of the card.
Title plate border treatment drifts across families — the set-verse plate carries a dark green-tinted outer stroke the other plates lack.

No ground plane: cards float on an abstract striped olive gradient with only a faint uniform shadow. Lighting/material integration is essentially flat, so the staging reads as a UI mockup rather than photographed physical objects.
The amber rail is asymmetric — a wide bar on the right, nearly nothing on the left — reading as a misregistered backing layer rather than an intentional frame construction.
The art window is mostly empty plum space; the small wall illustration floats low with no anchor, leaving the top half of the window dead. Weakest illustration of the set.
Monospace UI numerals (40/60) and the slashed/dotted zero on the cost badge read as debug-console type, tonally off against the Alegreya serif used everywhere else.
Radial sunburst shows visible banding between spokes; crescent accent strokes are asymmetric top-right vs bottom-left, slightly unbalancing an otherwise clean emblem.
The CAST VERSE ribbon overlaps the art window edge with an ambiguous half-in/half-out registration, and the nameplate drop shadow is heavy relative to the otherwise flat material language.
